title: February statements cover 30 days and spill into March
details:
Finance caught this while closing the February books.

The February 2024 merchant statement is labelled 2024-02-01..2024-03-02. It includes the 1st and 2nd of
March, and those same two days appear again on the March statement, so every affected merchant has two
days of transactions counted twice across the two documents.

April is wrong in the same way (2024-04-01..2024-05-01) and so is June, September and November. January,
March, May, July, August, October and December all look correct.

The pattern is that any month that does not have 31 days is wrong, and it is wrong by exactly the
difference. A statement period should start on the first of the month and end on the last day of THAT
month, whatever the month's length and whether or not it is a leap year.
